Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

attack verb and noun

with force

also an attack, assault, set upon, go for, charge (in battle), be attacked

classical

Liv. 21.58.3: adeō atrōx adorta tempestās est
Traupman 274

adorior, adorīrī, adortus sum

verb, fourth conjugation, deponent, transitive

attack, fall upon

Also of storms that fall upon someone.

Other words

  • aggredior, aggredī, aggressus sum — attack; set about

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.12.3: eōs impedītōs et inopīnantēs adgressus

    Properly “go up to”; also of approaching a person or tackling a task (see approach).

  • invādō, invādere, invāsī, invāsum — rush at, fall on

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 104.6: in pāscuum ēmissus cibum meum invāsī

  • oppugnō, oppugnāre, oppugnāvī, oppugnātum — attack, storm (a town, a camp)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 188: oppidum oppugnāre, to storm a town; Traupman 274

  • impetus, impetūs m. — an attack, a charge

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Liv. 2.10.4: sē impetum hostium … exceptūrum; Traupman 274

    To make an attack on: impetum facere in with the accusative. An attack of illness is also impetus (Traupman 62, 274).

Examples

  • Eōs impedītōs et inopīnantēs adgressus magnam partem eōrum concīdit

    He attacked them while they were encumbered and off their guard, and cut down a great part of themCaes. BG 1.12.3

  • adeō atrōx adorta tempestās est, ut Alpium prope foeditātem superāverit

    so fierce a storm fell on them that it almost outdid the horrors of the AlpsLiv. 21.58.3

  • sē impetum hostium, quantum corpore ūnō posset obsistī, exceptūrum

    he would take the enemy’s attack himself, as far as one body could hold it backLiv. 2.10.4

See also attack, enemy, war, approach.
